entry.title: fix: cap what one step can contribute to active time
entry.content:
fix: cap what one step can contribute to active time

active_ms was wall-clock between showing a step and answering it, uncapped.
That is only "active" while the learner is looking at the screen — a locked
phone, a tab switch or a metro stop accrued the whole gap.

Two things read that number. streak.session_counts accepts twelve active
minutes as an alternative to answering 60% of the plan, so uncapped, one tap
and a long gap and a second tap earn the day on two answers.
stats_service.minutes_7d reports it as study time.

This belongs with the tab fix: keeping SessionRunner mounted means a shown
step now survives tab switches by design, which is right for the bug being
fixed and makes this path strictly easier to reach.

Two minutes per step. The plan budgets about eight seconds a step, so a
learner who reads the mnemonic, thinks, and comes back is still well inside
it, while a forgotten screen contributes two minutes rather than two hours.

The test fails without the cap; checked. No existing active_ms values are
edited — they are the record of what happened.

Also corrects the _recent_sessions comment, which had the rationale
backwards. _finished_under_target gates a +1 *bump*, and only above 0.92
7-day retention, so the phantom sittings were making an extra syllable
marginally more likely, not shrinking the plan. The kind == daily filter is
still right: a 40-second drill is not evidence of finishing a lesson with
time to spare.

And todays_daily now uses one_or_none, so if 0004_one_daily_per_day's
uniqueness ever stops holding this fails loudly instead of silently picking
a row.

entry.title: feat: show what claiming syllables does, and why an empty day is empty
entry.content:
feat: show what claiming syllables does, and why an empty day is empty

Claiming ~46 syllables queues ~92 verification cards at 12 a day, so roughly
eight days of reviews starting tomorrow. That is good behaviour and the
learner was told none of it — she ticked a box and the next fortnight
changed shape.

"Знаю все" now previews first: how many syllables, how many cards, that they
are queued for checking rather than skipped, roughly how many per day and
for how long, and how many are left alone because she has already been
tested on them. The numbers come from a `preview` that walks the same items
and the same already-reviewed skip as `mark_known`, so what she agrees to is
what happens — a test asserts the two agree rather than trusting it.

Single cells stay a direct toggle, and the hint now says so: tapping a
claimed syllable again clears the claim and asks to be tested. That path
already existed in `unmark_known`, which refuses to touch a card carrying a
review log; nothing here weakens that.

The finished screen said "На сегодня всё" and stopped, which reads as a dead
end — worst for someone who has just claimed forty syllables and cannot see
them queued. It now says how many cards come back tomorrow, or when the next
one is due. Counted in the learner's own local day, so "tomorrow" means what
she means.

Three tests in test_practice_sessions encoded the old "any call yields
practice" contract; updated to ask for practice explicitly. The locked-door
test now asserts both halves: coming back hands the finished lesson back,
tapping for practice creates one.

Also fixes `make openapi`, which redirected to $(BACKEND)/openapi.json from
inside backend/ and had been writing to a directory that does not exist.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

entry.title: feat: /diag, so production can be inspected from a phone
entry.content:
feat: /diag, so production can be inspected from a phone

The duplicate-practice bug took a day to find, and every question along the
way — how big was her plan, did tapping around create sittings, how many
syllables are claimed but unchecked — needed a laptop with psql. The owner
is usually holding a phone.

Admin-gated, read-only, one message: per learner the timezone and targets,
cards by FSRS state, due-now, claimed-but-unverified, and today's sittings
with kind, outcome and planned/completed steps. Plus item counts by type
with how many are active, which is how an empty `kana` table would announce
itself instead of presenting as "the lesson is broken".

Each learner's own local date decides which sittings count. A test pins that
at an instant where Tokyo and Los Angeles are on different dates — my first
attempt picked 09:00 UTC, which is the same day in both, so it proved
nothing.

No message content, no answers, not even a first name: a test asserts the
learner's name does not appear, because the whole point is that this output
is safe to read in a chat.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

entry.title: fix: the tab bar wraps instead of widening the page
entry.content:
fix: the tab bar wraps instead of widening the page

.tabs was a plain flex row with no wrap. Flex items default to
min-width:auto, so four pills — five for an admin — could not shrink below
their text and pushed the row past the viewport, dragging the whole page
wider. Every horizontal scroll she hit came from here.

Wrapping rather than scrolling, because a scroller hides tabs a learner has
no reason to go looking for.

Measured in a browser at both widths rather than eyeballed. At 320px, the
narrowest phone worth supporting: with the fix, two rows, all five pills
inside the viewport, scrollWidth == 320. Without it, one row and
`allInside: false` — the last pills sit outside and are unreachable.

That check also killed an overflow-x: hidden I had added to .screen: it made
the page stop widening while leaving those tabs clipped and untappable,
which is worse than the bug. Any future overflow should be visible, not
silently cropped.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

entry.title: fix: a tab change no longer restarts the lesson
entry.content:
fix: a tab change no longer restarts the lesson

App.tsx rendered SessionRunner behind `tab === 'today'`, so every switch away
unmounted it and every switch back remounted it — and SessionRunner starts
the sitting in a mount effect. Checking the progress tab and coming back was
therefore a request for a new session.

It stays mounted and hidden now, which also means it keeps its current step,
its revealed answer and its progress bar while the learner looks at her
stats, instead of starting over.

Extra practice loses its accidental trigger, so it gets a deliberate one: an
"Ещё повторение" button on the finished screen, calling the endpoint that
does create a sitting. Before, the only way to practise from the app was the
bug.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

entry.title: fix: opening the app no longer mints a practice sitting
entry.content:
fix: opening the app no longer mints a practice sitting

The Mini App POSTs /api/session/today whenever its first tab mounts, and
switching tabs unmounts it. So a learner checking her progress and coming
back created a learning_sessions row every time. Practice draws from due
cards, and kana introduced minutes earlier are still in FSRS learning steps
measured in minutes — so the same syllables came round again in the same
order. Production shows three such sittings inside three minutes.

start_or_resume now treats "what should I be doing" and "give me more work"
as different questions. Without want=practice it hands back today's finished
lesson as-is: a session with no current step, which is the truthful answer.
Only want=practice creates anything, which is what /review and
/api/session/practice already pass.

Also filters _recent_sessions to daily. It feeds _finished_under_target,
which shrinks tomorrow's plan when recent sittings ran short — and practice
sittings are short by construction, a handful of due cards, often under a
minute. Counting them read a learner who did her full lesson *and* extra
practice as someone who keeps running out of time.

Both tests fail when their fix is reverted; checked, not assumed.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

entry.title: fix: uvicorn was running without --proxy-headers in production
entry.content:
fix: uvicorn was running without --proxy-headers in production

Found by deploying. The api command used a folded ">" scalar:

    command: >
      sh -c "alembic upgrade head &&
             uvicorn ... --port 8000
                     --proxy-headers --forwarded-allow-ips='*' --no-server-header"

A folded scalar collapses newlines only between lines at the same
indentation; a *more indented* line keeps its newline. So sh received three
lines, ran `alembic && uvicorn ... --port 8000`, and then tried to execute
`--proxy-headers --forwarded-allow-ips='*' --no-server-header` as a command
of its own:

    sh: 3: --proxy-headers: not found

Three consequences, none of which announce themselves:

* uvicorn ran **without --proxy-headers**, so X-Forwarded-Proto from Caddy
  was ignored — the app saw every request as http and every client IP as
  Caddy's container address.
* --no-server-header was dropped too, so the upstream Server header leaked.
* sh exited 127 after uvicorn died, replacing uvicorn's real exit code. The
  container reported "Restarting (127)" no matter what actually went wrong,
  which is how this hid.

One line now, and `exec` so uvicorn replaces sh and receives SIGTERM
directly instead of sh swallowing it and compose waiting out the kill
timeout.

`docker compose config -q` validates this file happily, which is why CI
never saw it — so CI now also rejects any multi-line service command.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

entry.title: chore: drop a git bundle that was committed by accident
entry.content:
chore: drop a git bundle that was committed by accident

27efcf2 staged nihongotutorphase0skeleton.bundle along with its intended
changes — my mistake, a `git add -A` over a working directory that had the
bundle sitting untracked in it. 174 KB of packed git history, checked into
git.

Nothing sensitive: it is this repository's own Phase 0 history, already
public here. But bundles are how work moves between machines, not source,
so *.bundle is ignored now to stop the next one following it in.

The blob stays in history; rewriting main to excise 174 KB is not worth
invalidating every existing clone.

entry.title: plan: reach Claude through Vertex, and STT through Google
entry.content:
plan: reach Claude through Vertex, and STT through Google

Direct Anthropic billing is not available to the owner, and neither is
OpenAI's, so two of the plan's AI decisions were unreachable as written.
Claude now goes through Vertex AI and STT through Google Cloud
Speech-to-Text v2. Both authenticate with the same service account that
already does TTS, so no Anthropic or OpenAI key exists anywhere in the
deployment — one credential, one vendor.

Vertex costs two things, and neither announces itself:

Server-side `fallbacks` is first-party only, so a refusal on Vertex would
have been a dead end. build_async_client registers the SDK's
BetaRefusalFallbackMiddleware instead, which needs an explicit fallback
model because there is no "default" routing policy to defer to. The
first-party path keeps the server-side parameter; sending it to Vertex
would be an error, so the client tracks which route it is on.

The Message Batches API is also unavailable, so offline seed generation
pays full price rather than the 50% batch rate. Recorded in the plan
against the task table that assumed the discount.

STT v2 takes OGG_OPUS natively — no transcode — and its PhraseSet
adaptation replaces OpenAI's `prompt=<target sentence>` trick. 60 min/month
free. openai_api_key is now dead config and is gone rather than left to
invite someone to fill it in.

Class names, the middleware signature, and the batches and fallback
availability were checked against anthropic 1.4.0 as installed, not
recalled.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

entry.title: content: put kanji in the examples, and use the plan's field names
entry.content:
content: put kanji in the examples, and use the plan's field names

All 93 example sentences were kana-only while 69 of the 93 headwords carried
kanji. That made example.reading a byte-for-byte copy of example.ja in every
single row, and left the furigana toggle — which the plan turns on by default
from the first vocabulary item — with nothing to render. 89 of the 93 now
carry kanji; the four that do not are the ones whose headword is kana or
katakana.

No new vocabulary enters the sentences: every word was already there in kana,
so this writes the same Japanese properly rather than making it harder. The
examples stay at the `core` stage, where kanji is correct — the kana seeds
are untouched, because the plan's validation gate requires kana-only text
during the bootcamp.

Verified the readings rather than trusting the rewrite: Sudachi reproduces the
pinned reading on 86 of 93 and disagrees on seven — 明日 as あす, 私 as
わたくし, 日本 as にっぽん, 四人 as よんにん, 何時 as なんどき. Each is a real
reading of the characters and the wrong one for this course, which is the
argument for authoring `reading` instead of deriving it. Recorded in
CONTENT.md, since it is the same case the audio section makes.

`source`/`reviewed` were invented names for concepts vocab_lemmas already
defines: now gloss_source ("claude") and gloss_review_status ("needs_review").

Three sentences were duplicated across entries (39/63, 46/68, 13/90, 40/91);
they are distinct now. Four first-person past-tense glosses forced a gender in
Russian — those sentences moved to the present tense, and the remaining
gendered glosses are neutral, since two learners of different genders share
this content.

entry.title: fix: carry the optimiser weights and the budget across as well
entry.content:
fix: carry the optimiser weights and the budget across as well

The learner block claimed to move the learner's settings and moved all but
two of them. daily_budget_usd is cheap to lose — it is one number a learner
can re-enter. fsrs_params is not: it is the personalised FSRS weight vector
the monthly optimiser produces, and the only way to reproduce it is to have
done the reviews again.

Nothing writes fsrs_params yet (Phase 4), which is what made it easy to
miss: a column that is null everywhere transfers correctly by accident, and
the day it stops being null is the day the loss becomes real and silent.
That is the worst possible shape for a bug in a tool whose entire job is not
losing state.

Both read with .get on import, so a payload written before they existed
still applies, and a learner whose optimiser has never run is left alone
rather than having null written over a default.

The round-trip test now sets a 21-float weight vector and asserts it lands.
Dropping the export line again fails it.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
